title: Mousambi (Sweet Lime): modeled ₹485/qtl left, Kullu → Hamirpur (Nadaun)
summary: January 2022: reported mousambi (Sweet Lime) prices at Kullu and Hamirpur (Nadaun) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 95% of 21 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹485 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 24 same-variety market pairs screened for mousambi (Sweet Lime) in January 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Hamirpur (Nadaun) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2022
scenes.caption: Kullu (Himachal Pradesh) and Hamirpur (Nadaun) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported mousambi (Sweet Lime) prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) on 21 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kullu reported a median ₹4,200 per quintal. Hamirpur (Nadaun) reported a median ₹5,250 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹975/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹975 per quintal, and Hamirpur (Nadaun) was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 161 km by road
scenes.caption: 161 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~3 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹35/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹451 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹181 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Hamirpur (Nadaun) report, the rule selects 21 of 21 modeled shipping days. 20 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹485 per quintal (₹215 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Mousambi (Sweet Lime) route from Kullu to Hamirpur (Nadaun) was positive on 95% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹48,500, or ₹21,500 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to mousambi (Sweet Lime)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹35/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Mousambi (Sweet Lime) route from Kullu to Hamirpur (Nadaun) was positive on 95% of matched days in January 2022. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹48,500, or ₹21,500 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Mousambi (Sweet Lime): modeled ₹1,151/qtl left, Naraingarh → Una
summary: December 2022: reported mousambi (Sweet Lime) prices at Naraingarh and Una imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 80% of 20 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹1,151 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 98 same-variety market pairs screened for mousambi (Sweet Lime) in December 2022; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Mousambi, Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Una report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.
